title: FMB Daily Brief — September 24, 2026
deck: Filipinos start Thursday watching Tropical Storm Surigae east of the country, a weaker Philippine growth outlook, new UK-backed project financing, and a major electronic-invoicing deadline for businesses.

hero.caption: Thursday morning edition. No documentary image is used where reuse rights have not been established.

stories.headline: Tropical Storm Surigae strengthens east of the Philippines; trough brings rain to parts of Visayas and Mindanao
stories.deck: The cyclone remains outside the Philippine area of responsibility, but its trough is already affecting eastern sections of the country.
body: ABS-CBN News reported shortly after midnight that the tropical depression east of the country had intensified into a tropical storm. GMA News, citing PAGASA's early-Thursday forecast, identified the system as Tropical Storm Surigae and placed it about 1,500 kilometers east of Northern Luzon at 3 a.m., moving west-northwest at 30 km/h with maximum sustained winds of 75 km/h.

GMA News said Biliran, Leyte, Southern Leyte, Dinagat Islands, Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur could see cloudy skies with scattered rain and thunderstorms from the trough. Metro Manila and most of the rest of the country face localized thunderstorms.
Why it matters: rain hazards can develop before a cyclone enters PAR, affecting travel, agriculture and flood- or landslide-prone communities.
What to watch: PAGASA track and intensity updates, any change in the system's PAR outlook, and local thunderstorm, flood or landslide advisories through Thursday.

stories.headline: ADB cuts Philippine 2026 growth forecast to 3.3%
stories.deck: The Manila-based lender sees weaker investment, costly imported fuel and fertilizer, and severe dry weather weighing on the economy.
body: GMA News reported that the Asian Development Bank lowered its Philippine GDP growth forecast for 2026 to 3.3% from 3.8%, while its 2027 forecast was reduced to 5.1% from 5.3%.
ADB cited the prolonged Middle East conflict, weaker first-half investment, higher prices for imported fuel and fertilizer, and severe dry weather associated with El Niño.
Why it matters: slower growth affects hiring, business expansion, government revenues and household purchasing power.
What to watch: subsequent official GDP data, inflation and fuel prices, investment indicators, and whether weather conditions further affect agriculture and food supply.

stories.headline: Philippines and UK open pathway for up to £5 billion in project financing
stories.deck: The two governments will identify projects that can tap British financing, expertise, goods and services.
body: ABS-CBN News reported that the Philippines and United Kingdom signed a partnership providing access to up to £5 billion, about P419.9 billion, in funding for government projects.
The UK is also part of the Luzon Economic Corridor initiative, with potential participation in connectivity, energy, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing supply chains.
Why it matters: the financing pool could expand infrastructure and investment capacity.
What to watch: which projects are selected, financing terms, procurement requirements, implementation timelines and the amount ultimately drawn.

sources.label: ABS-CBN News — Philippines signs deal for up to £5 billion funding from UK

stories.headline: BIR issues electronic-invoicing rules ahead of December 31 deadline
stories.deck: Covered e-commerce businesses and taxpayers using computerized accounting or invoicing systems face a major year-end compliance transition.
body: ABS-CBN News reported that the Bureau of Internal Revenue issued Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 98-2026 setting implementing rules for mandatory electronic invoicing, with a December 31 compliance deadline for covered taxpayers.

The rules cover small, medium and large businesses engaged in e-commerce and internet transactions, taxpayers under the Large Taxpayers Service, and businesses using computerized accounting systems or invoicing software. Micro enterprises are exempt from the mandatory requirement, according to the report.
Why it matters: the change affects how a large share of Philippine digital and formal businesses document sales and interact with the tax system.
What to watch: BIR implementation guidance, system integration requirements, transition support and enforcement after the deadline.
